_comment: Config for the `institutional` resolver (grey-literature / institutional reports). Everything here is data, editable without touching code. NO institution names are hardcoded in the resolver: identity comes from the citation itself, authority from the domain CLASSES below.
_authoritative_tlds_comment: A result domain ending in one of these TLDs (including multi-label public suffixes like `.gov.uk`, `.edu.au`) is treated as an authoritative primary source. Matched as a dotted suffix on the host.
_authoritative_domain_patterns_comment: Governmental / inter-governmental domains that do NOT carry an authoritative TLD (many IGOs sit on `.org`). A result host that equals or is a subdomain of one of these is authoritative. Add/remove freely; this is not a detection list for institutions, only a trust-class list for domains.
_org_author_words_comment: If the citation's leading author block contains one of these words, the author is an organisation, not a person. Detection signal #1.
_acronym_comment: An all-caps token of length in [acronym_min_len, acronym_max_len] in the author block (optionally with a spelled-out expansion in parentheses) is an organisational-author signal. Detection signal #2.
_report_like_words_comment: If the title/type looks like grey-literature output, that is detection signal #3 (an organisational author is still required for a positive detection).
_title_overlap_min_comment: Minimum overlap between the cited title and a candidate web result's title/page for the result to be accepted as the same report.
_max_results_comment: How many web-search results to consider per lookup.
_min_title_words_comment: Do not run a web lookup on a title shorter than this (too generic).
